title: Why So Many Temples?
intro: Kyoto kept the old capital’s job: houses for gods and for monks.
task: Count how many temple or shrine roofs you can see from one street.
reveal: Emperors sat here for centuries. Temples and shrines stacked up around the court.

moreInfo.title: A long capital
moreInfo.text: Kyoto was the imperial seat for about a thousand years. Power later moved. The religious houses stayed. Confirm the date range before live.

title: Shrine or Temple?
intro: At the next holy place, decide: shrine or temple? Use what you can see.
task: At the next holy place, decide: shrine or temple? Use what you can see.
reveal: Shrines are Shinto. Temples are Buddhist. The clues overlap. Guess, then check the name.
observeWhat: Torii, rope, foxes, incense, cemetery, Buddha.

title: Green Everywhere
intro: Find three matcha foods. Choose one to try.
task: Find three matcha foods. Choose one to try.

title: What Is Yatsuhashi?
intro: Before tasting, predict: chewy, crisp, sweet, cinnamon?
task: Before tasting, predict: chewy, crisp, sweet, cinnamon?
reveal: Often a cinnamon rice dough, raw-chewy or baked crisp. Recipes vary.

title: Where Is the Silver?
intro: Walk the pavilion. Find the silver.
task: Walk the pavilion. Find the silver.
reveal: There is no silver skin. The name came later, as a pair with the Golden Pavilion.

title: Gold vs Silver
intro: Which feels richer: gold leaf in the sun, or this quieter garden?
task: Which feels richer: gold leaf in the sun, or this quieter garden?
reveal: There is no right answer. Japanese gardens often prize restraint. Do not turn that into a slogan.

title: The Shogun Who Preferred Beauty
intro: A shogun who lost a war still shaped how Kyoto looks at beauty.
task: A shogun who lost a war still shaped how Kyoto looks at beauty.
reveal: Beauty here is a leftover of power, not a replacement for it.

moreInfo.title: Higashiyama
moreInfo.text: Ashikaga Yoshimasa lived here in retreat. Tea, gardens and quiet rooms grew around him. He was not a cartoon of peace. Confirm names and dates before live.
moreInfo.audioText: Ashikaga Yoshimasa was a shogun who lost control of a war and still left Kyoto a taste for quiet rooms, tea and gardens. Call that Higashiyama culture if you like. Do not make him a simple saint. We will check the history before this is live.

title: Spot the Machiya
intro: Find a house that is skinny on the street and seems to go far back.
task: Find a house that is skinny on the street and seems to go far back.
reveal: Machiya are townhouses: a small face, a long body.

moreInfo.title: The front
moreInfo.text: People often say a narrow front paid less tax. Treat that as a story to check, not a fact, until a source is attached.

title: Maiko or Tourist?
intro: If you see someone in geiko or maiko dress, do not chase them for a photo. Watch from a distance. Ask: working person, or visitor in costume?
task: If you see someone in geiko or maiko dress, do not chase them for a photo. Watch from a distance. Ask: working person, or visitor in costume?
reveal: This is a workplace. Respect beats a picture.

moreInfo.title: How to look
moreInfo.text: Do not block the street. Do not touch. Do not follow. A posed tourist in rented clothes is not a hunt target either.

title: Why Gion Exists Here
intro: Stand near Yasaka and look toward the lanes of food and inns. Who was this street for?
task: Stand near Yasaka and look toward the lanes of food and inns. Who was this street for?
reveal: Shrine visitors needed food, beds and shows. Gion grew to serve them.

title: Is It Actually Gold?
intro: The gold you see is paint.
task: The gold you see is paint.
reveal: It is real gold leaf on the upper floors.

title: Find the Bird
intro: Find the bird on the roof. Do not look at a photo first.
task: Find the bird on the roof. Do not look at a photo first.
reveal: A phoenix. Check the exact meaning before we print it.

title: The Temple That Burned
intro: Rebuilt in 1955. The gold is later care, not untouched medieval skin.
task: Rebuilt in 1955. The gold is later care, not untouched medieval skin.
reveal: Rebuilt in 1955. The gold is later care, not untouched medieval skin.

storySteps.text: The pavilion you see is not the first.
In 1950 a young monk set it on fire.
What you walk around was rebuilt.
